verdict.rationale: three.js is itself a JavaScript library, so its scripting language is the engine API. Community reports describe it as user-friendly, JS-accessible and working with TypeScript, though some @types/three signatures don't match the code. Debugger support rests only on a bare 'devtools' link (a Chrome extension) on threejs.org, with no documentation of its capabilities. Missing for 10: documented first-party debugger/inspector capabilities, accurate and maintained type definitions, independent corroboration of debugging workflow.

support.subject: As a game developer, the primary scripting language is productive and fully exposes the engine API, with a debugger behind it

citations.quote: Three.js is a cross-browser JavaScript library for creating 3D graphics using WebGL and WebGPU.
making GPU compute/rendering accessible via JavaScript on pretty much any device via the web browser
three.js works flawlessly with Typescript too
